column14: There is a weak negative association between smoking status and blood pressure (r = -0.13). The p-value of 0.16 is greater than 0.05, indicating that the association is not statistically significant. Therefore, smoking status does not show a significant relationship with blood pressure in this dataset.

The 30s age group has 4 outliers, while the 20s, 40s, 50s, and 60+ groups have no outliers. These outliers may increase the variability within the 30s group but are unlikely to affect the overall smoking–blood pressure correlation substantially.
Blood Pressure is approximately symmetric (skewness = 0.09). The 60+ age group has the highest variability based on IQR (28.00), while the 30s group has the lowest variability (8.65).

Point-Biserial correlation was appropriate because Smoking Status is a binary variable (Yes/No) and Blood Pressure is continuous. The correlation was r = -0.13 with p = 0.16, indicating a weak and statistically insignificant negative association.
The 30s age group had 4 blood pressure outliers. These may increase variability within that age group, but the overall smoking–blood pressure correlation remains weak and statistically insignificant.
